G1; Source gap; Executed credit agreements, indentures and receivables purchase agreements are not supplied; the filings list them as exhibits; MATERIAL; Covenant capacity, guarantee scope, collateral and recovery cannot be concluded; Supply the executed documents and amendments named in the exhibit list (10-K_2026-06-30_caci-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 104–105); Open

G2; Source gap; Covenant levels, reported covenant ratios and headroom are printed in no supplied document; only compliance is stated; MATERIAL; Covenant headroom not established; Supply a compliance certificate or the covenant definitions and levels; Open

G3; Source gap; Fiscal 2026 and the trailing twelve months to 2026-09-30 carry part-period acquisition earnings and no pro forma figures; MATERIAL; Leverage and coverage built on trailing earnings mix full acquisition debt with part-period earnings; Label any trailing measure; request acquired-business earnings for the pre-acquisition period; Open

G4; Source gap; Names of the subsidiary guarantors are not in the supplied text; MINOR; Structural priority by entity not established; Supply the guarantor schedules in the indenture and credit agreements; Open

G5; Source gap; No credit ratings, market quotes or peer data are supplied; MINOR; Ratings, market-implied and peer work not supported; not part of the selected work; Supply agency reports and dated quotes if those modules are wanted; Open

G6; Source gap; No maturity schedule at 2026-09-30; the latest schedule is at 2026-06-30 (10-K_2026-06-30_caci-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 89); MINOR; Maturity wall must be labelled as of 2026-06-30; Use the 2026-06-30 schedule with the quarter's scheduled payments labelled separately; Open

G7; Source gap; The term of the receivables-sale facility is stated as ending 2026-12-18 in older documents and not in the latest report (10-K_2026-06-30_caci-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 85); MINOR; Renewal status at the cutoff not established; Supply the latest amendment or the company's statement of renewal; Open

G8; Source gap; The proxy statement is not supplied; directors, executive officers, compensation and ownership are incorporated by reference (10-K_2026-06-30_caci-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 103); MINOR; Governance conclusions limited to the annual report; Supply the 2026 proxy statement; Open

G9; Source gap; No standalone quarterly report for the quarter ended 2025-09-30 and no earnings release for the quarter ended 2025-12-31; those figures appear as comparatives and in the December 2025 quarterly report; MINOR; None for totals; quarter detail rests on comparatives; None needed unless detail beyond comparatives is wanted; Open

G10; Conflict; ARKA purchase consideration USD 2,642.7 million in the annual report and USD 2,637.7 million in the September 2026 report; Not applicable; Explained by a USD 5.0 million refund recorded in the quarter; the allocation is still not final; Use USD 2,637.7 million for the latest date and label the earlier figure; Explained by the filing (calculation C6)

facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against reading leverage as still elevated is that the trailing figures carry the acquired business's debt for the whole period but only part of its earnings, since the acquisition closed on 9 March 2026 and no pro forma figures are supplied. A full-year earnings figure for the acquired business would lower both leverage ratios, and the company's guidance of at least USD 900 million of free cash flow for fiscal 2027, set against USD 725.96 million over the last twelve months, would cut net debt faster if delivered. The view would worsen if the receivables-sale facility lapsed without replacement, because up to USD 350.0 million of financing would leave the liquidity position, or if quarterly EBITDA stopped growing while cash interest stayed near its current level. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Revenue is concentrated in one customer but spread across agencies, which makes cash timing the main business risk rather than demand. Federal contracts supplied 95.6% of fiscal 2026 revenue, the Department of War 53.6% and the intelligence community 24.6%, and the ten largest contracts supplied 22.5% of revenue, or USD 2.2 billion, so no single program dominates. Continuing resolutions and shutdowns delay new programs and awards, and the government can terminate contracts for convenience, so a funding gap hits revenue timing and cash before it hits underlying demand. Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_caci-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 12, 50; 10-Q_2026-09-30_caci-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The contract mix is moving toward fixed-price work, which raises margin potential and cost-overrun risk together. Fixed-price contracts supplied 30.4% of fiscal 2026 revenue against 26.3% a year earlier, and 33.2% in the September 2026 quarter against 26.7% a year earlier, while cost-plus-fee contracts fell from 60.5% to 56.0% for the year and to 52.8% in the quarter. Direct costs fell to 64.6% of revenue in the quarter from 67.6%, which the company attributes to a favourable revenue mix, so the margin gain is the visible reward and an overrun on a fixed-price program is the exposure. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: A long-running civil action turned in the company's favour in October 2026 but is not finally closed. A jury verdict of USD 42 million in November 2024 was affirmed on appeal in March 2026, no amount was ever recognized, the Fourth Circuit directed dismissal in August 2026, and on 21 October 2026 the District Court vacated the judgment and dismissed the case, while the plaintiffs have said they may seek Supreme Court review. The amount is small against the company's liquidity, so the creditor consequence is limited to a tail risk and a second stayed suit that the District Court will dismiss or hold according to what the plaintiffs do. Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_caci-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 99; 10-Q_2026-09-30_caci-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 13, 30–31

facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against concern about acquisition-funded leverage is that the acquired businesses are being absorbed while the company still grew organically, margins widened and funded backlog rose, and that no distribution, waiver or exchange has been documented. If the company disclosed a leverage target, stated that further large purchases are paused until a ratio is reached, or supplied the debt documents showing tight limits on new debt and distributions, the view would move toward lower governance risk. The view would worsen if organic growth stayed near the September 2026 quarter's 2.1% while another debt-funded purchase was announced, or if the continuing resolution that funds the government to 11 December 2026 lapsed into a shutdown that delayed awards. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_caci-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17–18, 20; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_fy27-q1caci20261021ex991.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-K_2026-06-30_caci-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 46

facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence for a stronger credit view is that leverage fell from 4.18x at fiscal 2026 year-end to 3.92x within a quarter, that earnings of the acquired business are only partly counted so true run-rate leverage is lower, and that the backlog and margin trend are rising. The strongest evidence for a weaker view is that organic growth slowed to 2.1% in the September 2026 quarter and interest expense on an annualised basis implies cover of 4.21x. The view would improve if full-year earnings of the acquired business or covenant levels showed sufficient headroom, and worsen if the continuing resolution lapsed into a shutdown, the receivables-sale facility were not renewed, or a further debt-funded purchase were announced before leverage returned toward the fiscal 2025 level of 3.02x. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); EX-99.1_2026-10-21_fy27-q1caci20261021ex991.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation D1; calculation D6

facts.label: Cost structure and margin resilience
facts.text: Margins are defended by contract structure but exposed to the shift to fixed-price work. Direct costs of 66.80% of fiscal 2026 revenue are largely labour and subcontractors that cost-plus contracts pass through, which protects margin when volumes or wages move, while fixed-price work rose from 26.3% to 30.4% of revenue and to 33.2% in the latest quarter, so the company now carries more overrun risk for a higher margin. facts.label: Competitive forces
facts.text: Buyer power is high because essentially all contracts allow the government to terminate for convenience, and the customer sets contract terms, so a lost recompete removes revenue without recourse. Rivalry is intense with larger competitors and non-traditional entrants in cloud, cyber and satellite operations, which pressures pricing at recompete, while indirect competition from agencies doing work in-house limits the addressable market. Supplier power cannot be sized because subcontractor cost sits inside direct costs, but cleared labour is scarce, which raises wage cost, and in 9.91% of revenue the company is itself a subcontractor, so a prime contractor's cash problems can reach it; the threat of substitution appears low for classified mission work. facts.label: Downside scenario
facts.text: The initiating condition is a federal funding lapse when the continuing resolution ends on 11 December 2026. The first operational break is delayed new awards and program starts, which would slow growth beyond the 2.1% organic rate and could slow collections, since days sales outstanding already rose to 59 days. The financial transmission is lower operating cash flow while cash interest and scheduled principal continue, and if the receivables-sale facility were not renewed after 18 December 2026 up to USD 350.0 million of financing would need replacing. The liquidity consequence is a draw on the revolver from USD 605.00 million, but liquidity of USD 1,674.39 million is 4.78 times that facility, so the scenario does not point to liquidity distress, and leverage would rise only through lower EBITDA. Management levers are cutting acquisitions, repurchases and capital expenditure, and the observable triggers are the funding status after 11 December, revolver drawings and the receivables-sale renewal. ## Request

CACI INTERNATIONAL INC /DE/ (issuer id caci), as of 2026-11-05, credit snapshot pathway. The scope is whether the seven supplied issuer documents can support the selected work (Financial foundation, Business & governance and Fundamental credit) and what they cannot support. No credit conclusion is drawn here.
## Sources

No upstream analytical output was supplied: this module is the first of the run.
## Findings
### Bottom line

The seven supplied CACI filings and releases support the financial foundation, business and governance, and fundamental credit work through the quarter ended 30 September 2026, but they cannot support any covenant, ratings, market-pricing or portfolio conclusion. Creditors should treat covenant headroom, guarantee scope and recovery as not established until executed debt documents are supplied.

The statements are those of CACI International Inc consolidated, which is also the borrower or issuer of every printed debt instrument. The latest balance sheet, debt table and undrawn revolver of USD 1,395.0 million are filed figures, so liquidity can be built from the filings.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_caci-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 8–9, 21; calculation C1
### Key findings

Coverage of the latest period is complete for the statements the selected work needs. The quarter ended 30 September 2026 has a balance sheet, cash flow statement, segment results and a six-instrument debt table in the quarterly report, the earnings release repeats the statements, and the four discrete quarters from December 2025 to September 2026 are all present, which supports a last-twelve-months view. Revenue for the four fiscal 2026 quarters sums to the filed annual figure of USD 9,567.8 million.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_caci-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4, 8–9, 12; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_fy27-q1caci20261021ex991.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-K_2026-06-30_caci-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 66; calculation C7

Debt can be listed in full but cannot be tested against its covenants. Every instrument is printed with maturity, rate and balance at 30 September 2026 and 30 June 2026, and the principal amounts sum to the stated totals. The documents state compliance with all financial covenants at each balance-sheet date but print no covenant level, no reported ratio and no headroom, and only the December 2025 quarterly report even names the two tests, a maximum total net leverage ratio and a minimum interest coverage ratio.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_caci-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 8–9; 10-Q_2025-12-31_caci-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2026-06-30_caci-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 90; calculation C3; calculation C4; calculation C5

The perimeter is a holding company whose subsidiary guarantors are not named. CACI International Inc conducts operations through subsidiaries, the secured debt carries guarantees and collateral, and the guarantors appear only by reference to exhibits that are not supplied. The consolidated statements are therefore the only perimeter available, and structural priority cannot be read from the filings.

Fiscal 2026 earnings carry only part of the ARKA acquisition, and no pro forma figures are supplied. The acquisition closed on 9 March 2026 and was funded from increased borrowings and cash on hand, while the annual report states that pro forma results are not material and reports the acquired revenue only together with a smaller purchase. A trailing-twelve-month measure to September 2026 will therefore set the full acquisition debt against part-period earnings and must be labelled or adjusted.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_caci-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 79–81, 89; EX-99.1_2026-04-22_fy26-q3caci20260422ex991.htm.jsonl, page 5; calculation C6

The latest quarterly report omits two items that the annual report prints. It gives no maturity schedule at 30 September 2026, so the schedule at 30 June 2026 is the latest, and it does not state the term of the receivables-sale facility, which the annual report says runs to 18 December 2026. Near-term liquidity work must label both as older evidence.

Period labels need care because the Board approved a change to a calendar year on 20 October 2026. A six-month transition report to 31 December 2026 will follow, none is in the supplied set, and no supplied figure is affected. Labels must follow the company's June fiscal years until then.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_caci-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest case against calling the set limited is that the company states compliance with every financial covenant at each period end, shows USD 1,395.0 million undrawn on the revolver with no borrowings on the swing line or stand-by letters of credit, and prints a complete debt table, so a reader could say covenant levels add little. That case wins if the next filing prints the covenant levels and reported ratios, or if the executed credit agreement is supplied and shows ample headroom, in which case covenant capacity and structural priority move from not established to supported. The view would also change if a rating report or market quotes were supplied, because ratings and market-implied work would then become possible.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_caci-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 8–9, 21; calculation C1
### Limitations

- No executed credit agreement, indenture, supplemental indenture or receivables purchase agreement is supplied, so any conclusion on covenant capacity, guarantee scope, collateral or recovery stays not established and is never assumed from the filings' summaries.

- No credit ratings, market prices, quotes or peer data are supplied, so ratings, market-implied and peer-relative conclusions are not supported; only the change-of-control ratings-decline repurchase right is stated in the filings.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_caci-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 89
- No fund portfolio or mandate is supplied, so any portfolio-fit conclusion is outside what these sources can support.

- The earnings releases are issuer-prepared and their EBITDA, adjusted net income and free cash flow follow company definitions; they cannot override the filed statements, so conclusions on earnings quality rest on the filings first.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-21_fy27-q1caci20261021ex991.htm.jsonl, pages 9–11
- The proxy statement is not supplied, so governance conclusions on directors, executive officers, compensation and ownership are limited to the annual report's business and risk disclosures.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_caci-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 103
### Events: Sources

## Findings
### Bottom line

CACI's reported leverage is 3.92x total debt to LTM EBITDA at 30 September 2026, down from 4.18x at fiscal 2026 year-end but above the 3.02x of fiscal 2025, so creditors carry a debt-funded acquisition whose earnings are only partly in the numbers.

EBITDA covers cash interest 5.60x on the same basis against 6.67x at fiscal 2025 year-end, but only 4.21x against the quarter's interest expense annualised, and cash plus the undrawn revolver gives USD 1,674.39 million of liquidity against USD 46.75 million of fiscal 2027 principal scheduled at 30 June 2026. The leverage ratios use company-defined EBITDA with no pro forma credit for the acquired business, so they probably overstate run-rate leverage, and none of the ratios is a covenant measure.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_caci-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 8–9, 21; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_fy27-q1caci20261021ex991.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-K_2026-06-30_caci-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 66–67, 89; calculation C7; calculation C10; calculation C13; calculation C9; calculation C12; calculation C15; calculation C25; calculation C31
### Key findings

Leverage has eased from the acquisition peak but remains well above its pre-acquisition level. Total debt to EBITDA was 3.02x at fiscal 2025 year-end, 4.18x at fiscal 2026 year-end after the debt-funded ARKA purchase and 3.92x on the last twelve months to 30 September 2026, while net debt to EBITDA was 2.91x, 4.01x and 3.69x. Net debt fell by USD 153.08 million in the September 2026 quarter as the revolver was repaid and cash rose.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_caci-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 8–9; 10-K_2026-06-30_caci-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 66, 86–87; calculation C7; calculation C8; calculation C10; calculation C11; calculation C13; calculation C14; calculation C26

Interest cover has thinned since the acquisition, and the trailing cash figure flatters the current run-rate. EBITDA covered cash interest 6.67x in fiscal 2025, 5.49x in fiscal 2026 and 5.60x on the last twelve months to 30 September 2026, because cash interest paid rose from USD 145.04 million in fiscal 2025 to USD 213.64 million in fiscal 2026 on the larger debt stack. Cash interest paid was only USD 42.62 million in the September 2026 quarter because the notes' semi-annual coupons fall outside it, while interest expense and other, net was USD 73.24 million against USD 46.17 million a year earlier; four times that expense is USD 292.96 million, which would put cover at 4.21x.

Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_caci-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 66–67; 10-Q_2026-09-30_caci-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 4; 10-K_2026-06-30_caci-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 89; calculation C9; calculation C12; calculation C15; calculation C27; calculation C31
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against reading leverage as still elevated is that the trailing figures carry the acquired business's debt for the whole period but only part of its earnings, since the acquisition closed on 9 March 2026 and no pro forma figures are supplied. A full-year earnings figure for the acquired business would lower both leverage ratios, and the company's guidance of at least USD 900 million of free cash flow for fiscal 2027, set against USD 725.96 million over the last twelve months, would cut net debt faster if delivered. The view would worsen if the receivables-sale facility lapsed without replacement, because up to USD 350.0 million of financing would leave the liquidity position, or if quarterly EBITDA stopped growing while cash interest stayed near its current level.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_caci-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 79–81; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_fy27-q1caci20261021ex991.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5, 11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_caci-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 8; calculation C24
### Limitations

- Trailing leverage and interest cover set the full acquisition debt against part-period earnings of the acquired business, so they overstate run-rate leverage by an amount that cannot be sized from the supplied documents.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_caci-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 81; calculation C13
- The maturity ladder is drawn at 30 June 2026, so the fiscal 2027 and later amounts do not reflect the quarter's repayments, and no ladder at 30 September 2026 can be stated.
- The second-quarter fiscal 2026 EBITDA is derived from nine-month and quarterly figures because no release for that quarter is supplied, so the quarterly series carries one calculated point.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-04-22_fy26-q3caci20260422ex991.htm.jsonl, page 11; calculation C20
- No balance sheet at 30 September 2025 is supplied, so balance-sheet ratios cannot be compared with the same date a year earlier.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_caci-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3
- Covenant definitions are not supplied, so the leverage and cover ratios here are not the tests in the credit agreement and say nothing about headroom.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_caci-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 9

## Gaps

- High: Pre-acquisition earnings of the acquired business are not supplied for fiscal 2026 or the last twelve months, and the annual report calls the pro forma results not material, so leverage and interest cover cannot be restated pro forma; the action is to obtain the acquired business's earnings for the months before 9 March 2026.

- High: Covenant levels, reported covenant ratios and headroom are printed in no supplied document, so the ratios here cannot be tested against the credit agreement; the action is a compliance certificate or the agreement itself.

- Medium: No maturity ladder is printed at 30 September 2026, so the schedule at 30 June 2026 is used for fiscal 2027 and later years; the action is to take the quarter's repayments from the debt note and label the ladder.

- Medium: The term of the receivables-sale facility is stated only to 18 December 2026 in older documents and not in the latest quarterly report, so liquidity after that date is not established; the action is the latest amendment or a company statement.

- Medium: Margins, spreads, floors and the leverage-based pricing grid of the floating-rate debt are not printed, so rate sensitivity cannot be built from the instrument table; the action is the credit agreements.

- Medium: The legal ranking among the four secured facilities, and the names of the subsidiary guarantors, are not stated in the supplied documents, so the debt stack shows only the secured against unsecured order; the action is the guarantor schedules and the intercreditor terms.
- Low: The balance sheet at 30 September 2025 is not in the supplied documents, so the quarter-one fiscal 2026 column carries no balance sheet; the action is the quarterly report for that quarter.
- Low: Capital expenditure is printed as one total without a maintenance and growth split, so those sub-categories are not supplied; the action is management disclosure.

- Low: The filings print a dash for several cash flow lines in some periods, such as the divestiture lines, and the method treats a dash as missing rather than zero, so those cells carry the not-supplied wording.

- Low: Gross profit, cost of sales on a by-nature basis, interest income and exceptional items are not separate lines of the income statement, which prints interest expense and other as one net line; the action is the notes, where printed.

- Low: The carrying value of each debt instrument is not disclosed, only the total after one aggregate discount and issuance cost line, so the instrument table carries principal and a single financing cost adjustment.
- Low: The second-quarter fiscal 2026 EBITDA is derived because no release for that quarter is supplied; the action is the January 2026 release.
- Low: The revolving facility size at 30 June 2025 is not stated in the supplied documents, so undrawn capacity at that date is not supplied.

## Findings
### Bottom line

CACI is a diversified but federally dependent contractor with no sponsor or controlling owner disclosed in the supplied filings, so creditor risk rests on acquisition appetite and government funding timing, not on sponsor behaviour.

Federal agencies supply 95.6% of revenue and the largest customer group, the Department of War, supplies 53.6%. Two debt-funded acquisitions in two years, USD 1,681.9 million in fiscal 2025 and USD 2,642.7 million for ARKA in fiscal 2026, show a financial policy that favours growth by purchase over shareholder distributions, and the company has never paid a cash dividend.
### Key findings

Revenue is concentrated in one customer but spread across agencies, which makes cash timing the main business risk rather than demand. Federal contracts supplied 95.6% of fiscal 2026 revenue, the Department of War 53.6% and the intelligence community 24.6%, and the ten largest contracts supplied 22.5% of revenue, or USD 2.2 billion, so no single program dominates. Continuing resolutions and shutdowns delay new programs and awards, and the government can terminate contracts for convenience, so a funding gap hits revenue timing and cash before it hits underlying demand.

The contract mix is moving toward fixed-price work, which raises margin potential and cost-overrun risk together. Fixed-price contracts supplied 30.4% of fiscal 2026 revenue against 26.3% a year earlier, and 33.2% in the September 2026 quarter against 26.7% a year earlier, while cost-plus-fee contracts fell from 60.5% to 56.0% for the year and to 52.8% in the quarter. Direct costs fell to 64.6% of revenue in the quarter from 67.6%, which the company attributes to a favourable revenue mix, so the margin gain is the visible reward and an overrun on a fixed-price program is the exposure.

Backlog is large but only a small part is funded, and organic growth has slowed. Total backlog was USD 34.0 billion at 30 September 2026 and funded backlog USD 6.2 billion, 18.24% of the total, up from 15.93% a year earlier. Organic growth was 2.1% in the September 2026 quarter against 7.2% for fiscal 2026, so most of the quarter's 8.2% revenue growth came from acquisitions, while Department of War revenue rose 14.8% and federal civilian revenue fell 3.7%.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_caci-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 18, 20; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_fy27-q1caci20261021ex991.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 4; 10-K_2026-06-30_caci-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 50; calculation K10; calculation K11

Acquisition appetite is the main financial-policy signal, and it has been funded with debt. The company completed eight acquisitions in three fiscal years, three in fiscal 2025 for USD 1,681.9 million and ARKA in fiscal 2026 for USD 2,642.7 million net of cash acquired, funded from increased borrowings and cash, while principal debt rose by USD 1,988.50 million in fiscal 2026. Share repurchases fell from USD 168.56 million in fiscal 2025 to USD 17.08 million in fiscal 2026, which is consistent with cash being directed to acquisitions and debt service, and USD 187.3 million of the repurchase authorization remained at 30 September 2026.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_caci-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 67, 79, 82, 86; 10-Q_2026-09-30_caci-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12; calculation K6; calculation K8

Ownership and governance cannot be read as a sponsor case. The company is listed in New York with a small number of record holders, has never paid a cash dividend, and states a policy of retaining earnings, so no distribution or sponsor extraction is documented. The percentage held by any holder, the board's independence, related-party dealings and compensation sit in a proxy statement that is not supplied, so those questions are not established.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_caci-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 46, 103

Disclosure quality is good on the financial statements but thin on creditor protections. The auditor gave an unmodified opinion and found internal control effective, quarterly results are published within about three weeks of quarter end and annual results within about five weeks, and the debt note prints every instrument, but covenant levels, guarantor names and the legal ranking among secured facilities are not printed. A creditor can therefore monitor performance well and cannot test the debt documents' limits on further borrowing or distributions.

A long-running civil action turned in the company's favour in October 2026 but is not finally closed. A jury verdict of USD 42 million in November 2024 was affirmed on appeal in March 2026, no amount was ever recognized, the Fourth Circuit directed dismissal in August 2026, and on 21 October 2026 the District Court vacated the judgment and dismissed the case, while the plaintiffs have said they may seek Supreme Court review. The amount is small against the company's liquidity, so the creditor consequence is limited to a tail risk and a second stayed suit that the District Court will dismiss or hold according to what the plaintiffs do.
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against concern about acquisition-funded leverage is that the acquired businesses are being absorbed while the company still grew organically, margins widened and funded backlog rose, and that no distribution, waiver or exchange has been documented. If the company disclosed a leverage target, stated that further large purchases are paused until a ratio is reached, or supplied the debt documents showing tight limits on new debt and distributions, the view would move toward lower governance risk. The view would worsen if organic growth stayed near the September 2026 quarter's 2.1% while another debt-funded purchase was announced, or if the continuing resolution that funds the government to 11 December 2026 lapsed into a shutdown that delayed awards.
### Limitations

- No ownership percentages, board independence or compensation data are supplied, so the finding that no sponsor or controlling holder is disclosed rests on the filings' silence and could change if the proxy statement named a large holder.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_caci-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 103

- Legal capacity under the debt documents is not available, so the separation of what the company may do from what it has done cannot be made, and a low-risk reading of acquisition appetite cannot be tested against debt-incurrence limits.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_caci-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 88–89

- The acquired business's standalone earnings, synergies and integration costs are not disclosed beyond a combined post-acquisition contribution with a smaller purchase, so the leverage effect of acquisition appetite stays directional.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_caci-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 80–81
- Customer concentration is available by agency group and for the ten largest contracts but not by individual contract or agency, so the concentration finding could be sharper or weaker than stated.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_caci-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 50

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

ARKA Group L.P. was acquired on 9 March 2026 for USD 2,642.7 million net of cash acquired at 30 June 2026, later USD 2,637.7 million after a USD 5.0 million working-capital refund, and was funded from increased borrowings and cash on hand. The company had signed a commitment letter on 19 December 2025 for a senior secured bridge facility of up to USD 1,300.0 million, which stayed undrawn and ended on closing. The acquisition adds space-domain capability and, together with a smaller purchase, contributed USD 166.8 million of revenue in fiscal 2026. The pro forma results were judged not material by the company, so no combined earnings are available.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_caci-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 79–81; 10-Q_2026-09-30_caci-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; calculation K9

New debt was raised around the purchase. A Term Loan B-2 of USD 800.0 million, senior secured with guarantees and collateral identical to the existing Term Loan B, was added on 9 March 2026, and USD 500.0 million of additional 2033 senior unsecured notes were issued on 12 March 2026 at a premium for net proceeds of USD 516.5 million, used to repay revolver borrowings. The credit facility had been amended on 25 November 2025 to extend its maturity, with a revolver of USD 2,000.0 million and a term loan of USD 1,250.0 million, so the secured debt carries a majority of the company's assets as collateral while the notes sit behind it.

## Request

CACI INTERNATIONAL INC /DE/ (issuer id caci), as of 2026-11-05, credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the fundamental credit view: business quality, financial profile, downside path and monitoring, built on the seven supplied issuer documents and the earlier modules of this run.

## Findings
### Bottom line

CACI's fundamental credit profile is adequate: durable federal demand and USD 1,674.39 million of liquidity support creditors, but leverage of 3.92x after a debt-funded acquisition and dependence on federal funding timing mean deleveraging must come from free cash flow.

The main downside path is a federal funding disruption after the continuing resolution ends on 11 December 2026, delaying awards while debt service and the floating-rate cost of the acquisition debt continue. Free cash flow of USD 725.96 million over the last twelve months is 58.82% of EBITDA, and the company's guidance of at least USD 900 million for fiscal 2027 would speed repayment if met.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_caci-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_fy27-q1caci20261021ex991.htm.jsonl, page 5; calculation D1
### Key findings

The business profile is the strongest support. Revenue of USD 9,567.78 million in fiscal 2026 came almost entirely from federal agencies, backlog stood at USD 34.0 billion at 30 September 2026, and cost-plus contracts that pass cost increases to the customer supplied 56.0% of revenue, so demand and margin are well supported. Federal dependence also means no commercial customer can replace a lost agency, which is why funding timing, not demand, is the risk.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2026-06-30_caci-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 12, 52; 10-Q_2026-09-30_caci-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20

Leverage is the main financial constraint. Total debt was 3.92x EBITDA and net debt 3.69x at 30 September 2026 on a last-twelve-months basis, against 3.02x and 2.91x at fiscal 2025 year-end, because the acquisition added debt before its earnings were fully counted. Cash interest cover of 5.60x flatters the current burden, since the September 2026 quarter's interest expense annualised gives 4.21x.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation D1

Liquidity and the maturity profile leave no near-term refinancing pressure. Cash of USD 279.39 million plus USD 1,395.0 million of undrawn revolver gives USD 1,674.39 million against USD 46.75 million of principal scheduled for fiscal 2027, the revolver and term loan mature in November 2030, and the largest step, USD 1,706.75 million or 34.61% of principal, falls in fiscal 2031. The weakness is that the receivables-sale facility of up to USD 350.0 million has a stated term ending 18 December 2026 and its renewal is not established.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2026-06-30_caci-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 85, 89; calculation D1; calculation D2

Interest cost is the transmission channel from rates to cash flow. The floating-rate debt of USD 3,364.44 million is 41.61% covered by swaps of USD 1,400.0 million, and swaps of USD 350.0 million mature within twelve months, so each 100 bp move on the unhedged USD 1,964.44 million changes annual interest by about USD 19.64 million. That is small against EBITDA but compounds the leverage constraint if EBITDA stalls.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_caci-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 8–9; calculation D3; calculation D4

Cash conversion supports deleveraging if guidance is met. Operating cash flow excluding the receivables sale was 71.73% of fiscal 2026 EBITDA, and free cash flow over the last twelve months was 58.82% of EBITDA, so conversion is solid but was helped by lower cash taxes. Applying the guided USD 900 million of fiscal 2027 free cash flow to debt with EBITDA unchanged would bring net leverage from 3.69x to 2.96x, which is an illustration, not a forecast.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.1_2026-10-21_fy27-q1caci20261021ex991.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 11; calculation D5

Financial policy and governance are not the pressure point, but they are not established beyond the filings. No dividend or sponsor extraction is documented and repurchases are small, while acquisition appetite is the one behaviour that adds debt, and the executed debt documents that would show how far that can go are not supplied.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2026-06-30_caci-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 46, 88
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence for a stronger credit view is that leverage fell from 4.18x at fiscal 2026 year-end to 3.92x within a quarter, that earnings of the acquired business are only partly counted so true run-rate leverage is lower, and that the backlog and margin trend are rising. The strongest evidence for a weaker view is that organic growth slowed to 2.1% in the September 2026 quarter and interest expense on an annualised basis implies cover of 4.21x. The view would improve if full-year earnings of the acquired business or covenant levels showed sufficient headroom, and worsen if the continuing resolution lapsed into a shutdown, the receivables-sale facility were not renewed, or a further debt-funded purchase were announced before leverage returned toward the fiscal 2025 level of 3.02x.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); EX-99.1_2026-10-21_fy27-q1caci20261021ex991.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation D1; calculation D6
### Limitations

- No credit ratings, peer data or market quotes are supplied, so the profile cannot be set against typical leveraged-credit issuers in the sector and no rating view is given; the conclusion is absolute, not relative.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0)

- Covenant levels and the legal terms of the debt are not supplied, so the liquidity and leverage conclusions say nothing about headroom or capacity to add debt, and the financial policy assessment is behavioural only.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1)
- The downside path is qualitative and anchored on observed levels, because no source gives a stress threshold; the size of a funding disruption on cash flow is not established.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_caci-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17
- Pro forma earnings for the acquired business are not supplied, so the leverage ratios are stated as reported and the extent to which they overstate run-rate leverage is not established.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1)
### Strengths and weaknesses

The first strength is a demand base that is large and spread across agencies with which the company has long-term relationships. Federal agencies supplied 95.6% of fiscal 2026 revenue and total backlog of USD 34.0 billion, with funded backlog at 18.24% of it, gives revenue visibility that a funding delay can postpone but not remove, which supports debt service through a cycle.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_caci-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_caci-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; calculation K10; Business & governance (CP-1A)

The second strength is liquidity and a long maturity profile. Liquidity of USD 1,674.39 million against fiscal 2027 principal of USD 46.75 million, and a revolver and term loan that run to November 2030, mean the first refinancing event is some years away and a funding disruption would be met from available cash and the revolver.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation D1

The third strength is cost pass-through and rising margin. Cost-plus-fee work was 56.0% of fiscal 2026 revenue and the EBITDA margin rose from 11.21% in fiscal 2025 to 12.65% over the last twelve months, which supports interest cover as the debt stack grows.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_caci-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 52; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation D1
The fourth strength is financial policy that has not extracted cash. No dividend has ever been paid and repurchases fell sharply in fiscal 2026, so earnings have stayed available for debt service.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_caci-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 46, 67; Business & governance (CP-1A)

The first weakness is leverage after the acquisition. Total debt of 3.92x and net debt of 3.69x LTM EBITDA at 30 September 2026 are above the 3.02x and 2.91x of fiscal 2025 year-end, which reduces the cushion for creditors if earnings fall.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation D1

The second weakness is the dependence on federal funding timing. A continuing resolution funds the government to 11 December 2026 and a shutdown in the autumn of 2025 shows the risk is real, so a delay would hit awards and cash while debt service continues.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_caci-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17

The third weakness is interest cost and hedge roll-off. Floating-rate debt is only 41.61% hedged and USD 350.0 million of swaps mature within twelve months, so a rate rise passes quickly into interest cost at a time when cover is already lower on an annualised basis.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_caci-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 8–9; calculation D3; calculation D4

The fourth weakness is acquisition appetite combined with slowing organic growth. Organic growth was 2.1% in the September 2026 quarter against 7.2% for fiscal 2026, so growth has relied on purchases that are funded with debt.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-21_fy27-q1caci20261021ex991.htm.jsonl, page 2; Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Company description

CACI provides technology and expertise to national security customers in intelligence, defense and federal civilian agencies through a holding company with subsidiaries in the United States and Europe. Domestic Operations produced 96.8% of fiscal 2026 revenue, and the company grew through eight acquisitions in three fiscal years, the largest being ARKA in March 2026, which adds space-domain capability. Cash-flow visibility comes from long, multi-year contracts and a large backlog, so debt service is supported, while refinancing confidence depends on continued federal funding because no commercial customer base offsets it.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_caci-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 7, 9; Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Ownership and group structure

CACI International Inc is a listed holding company with no sponsor or controlling holder disclosed in the supplied documents, so there is no sponsor whose willingness to support or extract cash needs to be judged. Debt is issued or borrowed at the holding company with guarantors that are not named, which means structural priority cannot be read from the filings and is passed to the module that handles it. The financial policy evidence is a record of debt-funded acquisition, no dividend and falling repurchases.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_caci-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 46, 104; Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Revenue drivers and pricing power

Revenue is predictable but concentrated rather than recurring in the commercial sense. Federal agencies supplied 95.6% of revenue, the ten largest contracts 22.5%, and the company wins work by competitive bid, so growth comes from new awards and exercised options and not from pricing power. Total backlog includes unexercised options and only USD 6.2 billion is funded, so revenue beyond the funded work depends on appropriations, and organic growth of 2.1% in the latest quarter shows demand is steady rather than accelerating.
### Cost structure and margin resilience

Margins are defended by contract structure but exposed to the shift to fixed-price work. Direct costs of 66.80% of fiscal 2026 revenue are largely labour and subcontractors that cost-plus contracts pass through, which protects margin when volumes or wages move, while fixed-price work rose from 26.3% to 30.4% of revenue and to 33.2% in the latest quarter, so the company now carries more overrun risk for a higher margin. EBITDA grew 21.42% in fiscal 2026 against revenue growth of 10.89%, which shows operating leverage working upward and would work downward if revenue stalled.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_caci-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 52, 66; 10-Q_2026-09-30_caci-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 6; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation D7
### Capital intensity and cash conversion

Capital needs are light and cash conversion is the main support for deleveraging. Capital expenditure was 1.11% of fiscal 2026 revenue, so most operating cash flow is available for debt service, and free cash flow over the last twelve months was 58.82% of EBITDA. Cash interest and acquisition-related integration costs absorb the rest, and cash taxes fell in fiscal 2026, which means part of the conversion may not repeat.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2026-06-30_caci-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 67; calculation D1
### Competitive forces

Buyer power is high because essentially all contracts allow the government to terminate for convenience, and the customer sets contract terms, so a lost recompete removes revenue without recourse. Rivalry is intense with larger competitors and non-traditional entrants in cloud, cyber and satellite operations, which pressures pricing at recompete, while indirect competition from agencies doing work in-house limits the addressable market. Supplier power cannot be sized because subcontractor cost sits inside direct costs, but cleared labour is scarce, which raises wage cost, and in 9.91% of revenue the company is itself a subcontractor, so a prime contractor's cash problems can reach it; the threat of substitution appears low for classified mission work.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_caci-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_caci-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18; Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Policy and macro factors

Federal budget policy is the one macro factor that changes credit quality. Continuing resolutions delay new programs and awards, the reconciliation law made about USD 156 billion of defense funding available regardless of annual appropriations, and the government is funded only to 11 December 2026, so a lapse would test liquidity while longer-term funding looks supported. Interest rates matter through the floating-rate debt, and technology change is a revenue driver rather than a credit threat in the period reviewed.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_caci-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17; calculation D3
### Credit-translated SWOT

Strengths are the funded federal demand, backlog, cost pass-through and liquidity described above. Weaknesses are post-acquisition leverage, dependence on one customer, the fixed-price shift and interest cost. Opportunities that could improve credit quality are guided free cash flow of at least USD 900 million, margin expansion and conversion of the acquired space business into earnings that lower leverage. Threats that could weaken it are a funding lapse, a further debt-funded acquisition, non-renewal of the receivables-sale facility and loss of a large recompete.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-21_fy27-q1caci20261021ex991.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation D5
### Financial profile and credit quality

The financial profile is adequate and trending toward better leverage but not yet there. Scale is large with revenue of USD 9,567.78 million, margin is rising, liquidity is USD 1,674.39 million, and conversion supports repayment, while leverage of 3.92x and the cost of floating-rate debt constrain it. Refinancing capacity looks sound for the next several years because the nearest large maturity is in fiscal 2031, though capital-market access is judged only from that profile because ratings and market prices are not supplied. The missing datapoints that would sharpen the view are covenant levels, pro forma earnings and ratings.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation D1; calculation D8
### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

For the next twelve to twenty-four months the company guides fiscal 2027 revenue of USD 10,700 million to USD 10,900 million, which implies growth of 11.83% to 13.92% over fiscal 2026 once the full year of the acquired business is included, and free cash flow of at least USD 900 million. Tailwinds are the backlog, a 2.0x book-to-bill in the latest quarter, Department of War revenue growth of 14.8% and mandatory defense funding; headwinds are the 3.7% fall in federal civilian revenue, slowing organic growth and the funding lapse risk. Medium-term outlook over three to five years is not established, because the company states targets without figures in the supplied documents.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-21_fy27-q1caci20261021ex991.htm.jsonl, pages 1, 4–5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_caci-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18; calculation D9
### Downside scenario

The initiating condition is a federal funding lapse when the continuing resolution ends on 11 December 2026. The first operational break is delayed new awards and program starts, which would slow growth beyond the 2.1% organic rate and could slow collections, since days sales outstanding already rose to 59 days. The financial transmission is lower operating cash flow while cash interest and scheduled principal continue, and if the receivables-sale facility were not renewed after 18 December 2026 up to USD 350.0 million of financing would need replacing. The liquidity consequence is a draw on the revolver from USD 605.00 million, but liquidity of USD 1,674.39 million is 4.78 times that facility, so the scenario does not point to liquidity distress, and leverage would rise only through lower EBITDA. Management levers are cutting acquisitions, repurchases and capital expenditure, and the observable triggers are the funding status after 11 December, revolver drawings and the receivables-sale renewal.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_caci-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 16–17, 21; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_fy27-q1caci20261021ex991.htm.jsonl, page 2; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation D1; calculation D2
### Overall credit view

Overall, CACI presents a business profile that is large and supported by funded federal demand, but credit quality is constrained by leverage after a debt-funded acquisition. Cash-flow durability appears adequate due to cost pass-through, light capital needs and a rising margin. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on the next two to three years of free cash flow and on the November 2030 maturities. The primary downside path is a federal funding disruption that delays awards while interest on partly unhedged floating-rate debt continues. Further analysis would require covenant levels, pro forma earnings for the acquired business, and ratings and market prices. Top risk: federal funding timing.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation D1
